A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same complete 19-page study, including Appendices A–G. Text extraction and rendered-page comparison establish that the text, equations, figures, and tables support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v4 reports original experiments evaluating ten LLMs on CRUXEval and SemTrace, including positional effects, line-removal experiments, and multilingual results (Section 5; Appendices A–D).

after.justification: v5 retains the original experimental results on CRUXEval and SemTrace, including the main comparisons and smaller-model, error, and multilingual analyses.

M1.justification: The counterfactual line-removal procedure and SemTrace generation through randomized arithmetic assignments are identical in Sections 3.2–3.3. No method component changes.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same CRUXEval, SemTrace, and CodeSearchNet coverage across Python, JavaScript, and PHP, with the same retrieval and input/output prediction tasks.

E2.justification: The same ten evaluated LLMs, four-model multilingual subsets, and Python-interpreter reference remain in the corresponding experiments. No comparator is added or removed.

E3.justification: Section 4 retains the same sample sizes, GPT-4.1 subsampling, 20–80 distractors, eleven target positions, greedy decoding, prompting, and accuracy metrics. Appendix evaluation procedures also match.

E4.justification: The line-removal sensitivity experiment, higher-digit arithmetic analysis, partial-match analysis, and unresolved-output analysis are unchanged (Sections 5.2–5.3; Appendix C).

E5.justification: The exponential fitting and bootstrapped 95% confidence intervals in Figures 1 and 3 are unchanged. Neither version adds different run-count, seed, or significance reporting.

E6.justification: Numerical tables, plotted results, and qualitative findings match throughout. This includes the reported median accuracy drops of 92.73% for SemTrace and 53.36% for CRUXEval, plus all appendix results.

T1.justification: The recall definitions, semantic recall sensitivity formula in Equation 1, and SemTrace chance-guessing calculation are identical. No mathematical assumption, derivation, or proof changes.

C1.justification: The abstract, contributions, and conclusion retain the same claims about lexical–semantic recall dissociation, benchmark shortcuts, and SemTrace revealing underestimated positional failures.

C2.justification: Interpretations concerning pattern matching, arithmetic memorization, partial recall, and language differences are identical. The broader implications and limitations concerning distractors, task scope, arithmetic, context length, and benchmark scale also remain unchanged.

D1.justification: The code-access link, model and dataset licenses, prompt templates, hardware, software versions, and execution-time disclosures match (Section 4; Appendices E–G).

R1.justification: Related-work discussions, novelty positioning, and cited works are identical. No reference or substantive relationship to prior research is added or removed.

P1.justification: The arXiv margin stamp changes from v4 dated 20 April 2026 to v5 dated 10 July 2026. PDF title metadata changes from 'Code Reasoning' to 'Code Understanding,' matching the unchanged printed title; prose and document structure otherwise match.

P2.justification: Figures 1–14, Tables 1–4, Listing 1, captions, and page layout are unchanged. Rendered pages match apart from the version/date text in the first-page margin.

improvement.justification: The main text and appendices preserve the same scientific content, empirical evidence, explanations, limitations, and visual presentation. Updating the version/date stamp and aligning PDF title metadata does not meaningfully change overall paper quality.
